title: Snapshot_deletion threadpool active thread count stuck at 1 after encountering failure
body: After upgrading from OpenSearch 2.15.0 to 2.18.0, snapshot deletion sometimes leaves the snapshot_deletion thread-pool active count stuck above zero after warnings that blobs could not be deleted from our S3 repository. There are no pending cluster tasks. Restarting the cluster-manager node clears the active count, and the deleted snapshot is no longer listed, but the next deletion can become stuck again and report both new blobs and blobs from the previous deletion. The warnings list the affected blobs without an exception or cause. I expect the active count to return to zero even when deletion encounters a failure.

symptoms_visible: After a snapshot deletion logs 'Failed to delete following blobs', the snapshot_deletion active thread count sometimes remains above zero indefinitely.
There are no pending cluster tasks; restarting the cluster-manager node returns the active count to zero, but a later deletion can become stuck again and list both new and previously reported blobs.
The deleted snapshot is absent from the snapshot list even while the snapshot_deletion active count remains stuck.
N0.label: N0 stuck snapshot deletion workers reported

symptoms_visible: The active snapshot deletion count intermittently remains nonzero after scheduled deletions on our large production clusters.
N1.label: N1 production reproduction context collected

symptoms_visible: On the affected node the snapshot_deletion active count is stuck at 4, and the only snapshot-related logs are long lists of blobs that failed to delete without any accompanying exception.
N2.label: N2 thread dump and complete logging evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After upgrading the affected production clusters to 2.19.1, snapshot deletion threads still become stuck above zero with the same failed-blob warnings.
N2_x.label: N2_x newer maintenance release aftermath

symptoms_visible: For several days after upgrading to the build containing the snapshot deletion fix, the snapshot thread count has not become stuck again.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after fixed-build upgrade

question_patterns: Can you provide the steps and workload under which this occurs?
What snapshot schedule, retention settings, and cluster size are involved when the active count becomes stuck?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We run a snapshot management policy for the entire cluster at 12am and 12pm, with deletion at 2am and 2pm, retaining a minimum of 2 and maximum of 7 snapshots. After letting it run for a few days, the deletion count can remain nonzero. It is intermittent and so far appears only on our large production clusters, where some daily indices have 250 shards and are 3–4 TB.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can reproduce it immediately on a small empty cluster with a single manually created snapshot and a local filesystem repository.
The same intermittent behavior occurs with a slightly different retention maximum, but still only on our large scheduled snapshot workload.

edges.comment: Issue c1-c2, reporter's production system: the maintainer requested reproduction steps and the reporter updated the description with the policy schedule, retention, intermittency, and large-cluster characteristics.

question_patterns: Can you paste the complete message around the failed blob deletion and any nearby exceptions?
Are there any other snapshot-related exceptions in the logs at the time the active count becomes stuck?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The full warning is a very long list of blob tuples, so I only removed the middle portion that repeats more tuples. I did not find an exception in that message or any other snapshot-related exception around the same time; this is the only type of snapshot log line I see.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The surrounding logs contain a clear S3 access-denied exception for every failed delete request.
The tuple list contains different blob names, but there is still no exception or cause in nearby logs.

question_patterns: Can you capture a thread dump while the snapshot_deletion active count is stuck?
Please run jstack on an affected node while the active count is nonzero and share the snapshot_deletion thread stacks.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured and shared a thread dump while the snapshot deletion thread count was stuck at 4 on this node. The snapshot_deletion thread is in WAITING (parking), with BaseFuture.get, FutureUtils.get, AdapterActionFuture.actionGet, and BlobStoreRepository.deleteContainer in its stack.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The thread dump has no snapshot_deletion workers waiting in deleteContainer; all of them are idle and the nonzero metric has no corresponding active thread.
The count is stuck at 1 instead of 4, but its stack has the same WAITING state and deleteContainer frames.

edges.comment: Issue c5-c10 and c15-c21, reporter's affected cluster: maintainers requested the full warning, nearby exceptions, and a live thread dump. The reporter supplied raw log and stack output without identifying the underlying asynchronous-completion defect.

solution.intent: Try upgrading the affected production clusters to the then-current newer 2.x maintenance release in case the snapshot deletion hang has already been corrected.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade a tested cluster from 2.18.0 to 2.19.1 and observe whether scheduled snapshot deletion workers still remain active.

edges.comment: Issue c3-c4 and c12-c13, reporter's clusters: maintainers asked about a newer 2.x release; the reporter later upgraded the affected production clusters to 2.19.1 and confirmed that the stuck snapshot deletion behavior persisted. The unrelated connection-pool symptom disappeared, but it is deliberately excluded from this diagnostic chain.

solution.intent: Treat the nonzero count as real blocked snapshot deletion work, not a stale statistic: deploy a build containing the async snapshot deletion completion fix, preferably validate it outside production first, and monitor subsequent scheduled deletions before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: The live stack shows snapshot_deletion workers waiting through BaseFuture.get inside BlobStoreRepository.deleteContainer. Test OpenSearch 2.19.3 in pre-production, then roll it out because it contains the linked snapshot deletion fix despite its omission from the release notes. After deployment, monitor several scheduled deletion cycles and confirm that the active count returns to zero and no worker remains parked in deleteContainer.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied only the raw WAITING stack and the absence of accompanying exceptions. Maintainers inferred that the workers were genuinely blocked in BlobStoreRepository.deleteContainer while waiting for asynchronous deletion completion. The initially proposed whenComplete registration race was explicitly disproved in c20, so that specific race must not be presented as the accepted root cause.

edges.comment: Issue c14 and c19-c35, reporter's same production deployment: the dump established real workers blocked in deleteContainer; the first race hypothesis was withdrawn after testing. Maintainers linked a fix, stated that a later maintenance build contained it, and requested pre-production testing. The reporter upgraded and then reported that the stuck count had not recurred for several days.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted diagnosis at the level established by the thread: snapshot_deletion workers are genuinely blocked in BlobStoreRepository.deleteContainer while waiting for asynchronous S3 blob-deletion completion, rather than the active count merely being a stale statistic.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the live thread dump shows WAITING workers in BaseFuture.get and BlobStoreRepository.deleteContainer, while the blob-failure warnings and surrounding logs contain no explanatory exception.

Must not claim that the disproved completion-handler registration race is the root cause, and must not treat the earlier newer-maintenance-release upgrade as the fix because the reporter reproduced the stuck threads after that upgrade.
Must recommend deploying a build containing the snapshot deletion completion fix rather than relying on repeated cluster-manager restarts as the resolution.

Must ask the reporter to verify the result over subsequent snapshot deletion cycles on a build containing the fix before declaring the issue resolved; the thread's resolution is supported by the reporter observing no recurrence for several days after upgrading.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced OpenSearch production operator who manages large clusters, snapshot management policies, S3 repositories, upgrades, cluster APIs, logs, and JVM thread dumps.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, evidence-driven, and cautious about production changes; provides exact requests and raw diagnostics, answers follow-up questions directly, and asks for a concrete technical justification before upgrading production.
